'''Jean Ginibre''' (4 March 1938 — 26 March 2020)<ref>[http://smai.emath.fr/liste-smai/msg00879.html Death of C. Foias and J. Ginibre]</ref><ref>[http://www.iamp.org/bulletins/old-bulletins/Bulletin-Oct2021-print.pdf In Memoriam: Jean Ginibre (1938-2020). News Bulletin of the IAMP, October 2021]</ref><ref>[https://link.springer.com/collections/bagdbdeada Nonlinear Waves, Kinetic Theory and Related Topics: A Tribute to the Memory of Jean Ginibre]</ref> was a French [[mathematical physicist]]. He is known for his contributions to [[Random matrix| random matrix theory]] (see [[circular law]]), [[statistical mechanics]] (see [[FKG inequality]], [[Ginibre inequality]]), and [[partial differential equations]]. With Martine Le Berre and [[Yves Pomeau]], he provided a kinetic theory for the emission of photons by an atom maintained in an excited state by an intense field that creates [[Rabi oscillation]]s. He received the [[Paul Langevin Prize]] in 1969.<ref>[http://sfp.in2p3.fr/Prix/prix_anciens.html Webpage of the French Physics Society]</ref>

Jean Ginibre was Emeritus Professor at [[Paris-Sud 11 University]].<ref>[http://www.th.u-psud.fr/annuaire2.php3?fiche=jean.ginibre Webpage of Jean Ginibre at Paris-Sud 11]</ref> He directed the thesis of [[Monique Combescure]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Madame le Professeur Monique COMBESCURE |url=https://archive.wikiwix.com/cache/index2.php?url=http://www.academiecatholiquedefrance.fr/index.php/qui-sommes-nous/membrescorps-academique/82-section-i-medecine-sciences-de-la-vie-et-de-lunivers/11-madame-le-professeur-monique-combescure#federation=archive.wikiwix.com&tab=url |access-date=2022-09-22 |website=archive.wikiwix.com}}</ref>
